answer: Latency-fingerprint attestation ties each identity to a physical network location. Reference beacons near a jetty data center and an inlet cable landing continuously ping every registered agent; round-trip times form a stable geographic fingerprint. An attacker spawning clones must place each at a genuinely distinct site with its own hardware and broadband contract, since copying a fingerprint means matching microseconds of propagation delay. A zephyr-like duplicated latency pattern flags the cluster for slashing, making sybil farming cost real estate per identity, not just wallets.
